regime_context: Hong Kong thematic leadership is narrow: only 3 of 14 themes are eligible via the absolute-trend gate, led by Banks (unscorable) followed by High-Dividend and Industrials (also unscorable). The only scorable theme, China Tech & Internet, is ineligible and mid-ranked. Macro backdrop is dominated by geopolitical and monetary headlines with high unscheduled surprise share. Gate_helps is true, so trend-following discipline has historically cut drawdowns, but the rotation signal is display-only and momentum rank has no forward edge. Given zero track record, all lean conviction must be low.

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: The absolute-trend gate – the detector’s only validated edge – is designed for drawdown/shake-out avoidance by staying with themes in a positive trend. Banks is the top-ranked eligible theme, not crowded, and the macro backdrop (geopolitical/monetary surprises) favours defensive positioning. This lean is entirely a risk-control tilt, not a return forecast; the rank carries no alpha and the Hurst tag is mean-revert, so it is a fragile trend-following posture.
evidence: eligible=true (positive absolute trend, the validated risk-control leg)
macro_narrative: geopolitics + monetary surprise dominance supports defensive themes
theses.dissent: The Hurst exponent is mean-revert, suggesting the trend may not persist; the theme has no scorable ETF proxy to verify the signal; rank momentum has no predictive power; macro shocks (unscheduled share 1.0) could rapidly reverse the trend, causing whipsaw.

falsifier.text: If Banks (H + HK) lose eligibility (i.e., absolute trend turns negative, e.g., 50-day price momentum flips), the overweight rationale is invalidated.
